text.p: Tunisia has released a human rights activist and a leftist opponent of the government, both serving jail terms, lawyers said on Tuesday.

Tunisian barristers association head Abdelwahab Behi said lawyer Najib Hosni, whose case has been closely followed by international human rights groups Amnesty International and the Lawyers Committee for Human Rights, was freed on Saturday.
"He was released conditionally by a decision of President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali and at our association's call," Behi told Reuters.
"We welcome his release which is an ilustration of our association's role in boosting human rights in the country," he added.
Hosni, a human rights defender, was arrested in June 1994 and sentenced in January 1996 to eight years imprisonment on charges of forging a contract for a property sale.

Lawyers also said that Mohamed Hedi Sassi, arrested in April 1994 and sentenced to three years and four months jail for supporting a banned leftist movement Parti Ouvrier Communiste Tunisien (POCT) was also released conditionally.
Amnesty International welcomed the two releases but said it was concerned that the charges against the men have not been dropped.
"These men were imprisoned solely for their beliefs and should be released unconditionally," it said in a statement released by its headquarters in London.
